questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving, what should you do?

options.text: The vehicle should be running and in gear.
Do the check from inside the vehicle.
Check the lights using a reflection in a shiny surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: To check your lights, set the parking brake and turn off the engine. Remove the key and take it with you. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out and look at each light to make sure it works.

questions.question: When you start the engine, how long should oil pressure take to reach a normal level?
questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges when you start the engine. Oil pressure should reach a normal level within a few seconds.

questions.question: A convex mirror is sometimes called a ____ mirror.
questions.correctAnswerText: Bug-eye
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often have curved, convex mirrors called "bug-eye," "fisheye," or "spot" mirrors. These mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, what should you inspect?
questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with power steering, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Which tire setup is acceptable?

options.text: Dual tires that do not touch each other
Tires of different sizes if used only on short trips
Retreaded tires on the front of a school bus

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual tires that do not touch each other
questions.explanation: Dual tires must not touch each other or other vehicle parts. Tire sizes must match. Tires must not be cut or damaged. Retreaded or recapped tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: How fast should you take a highway curve?

options.text: At or slightly above the posted speed limit.
Well below the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have a high center of gravity and tip easily on curves. Take curves and ramps at speeds well below the posted limit.

questions.question: If other vehicles have trouble passing your truck on a road with two or more lanes, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use the right lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane if your heavy vehicle is slower than traffic. Let other vehicles pass you using the left lane.

questions.question: Is it good to keep space between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: Yes, it gives you time to react to hazards.
Only if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it gives you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep space cushions on all sides of your vehicle for safe driving. This gives you time to react if something goes wrong.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing during an inspection?

options.text: The driver can drive at reduced speeds.
The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is repaired.
The vehicle is fine since most of the spring is still there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is repaired.
questions.explanation: Check the suspension for broken or missing leaves. Missing leaves are dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from any leaf spring, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: When filling a tank divided by bulkheads with liquid cargo, what should you do?

options.text: Fill the front section the most.
Fill the rear section the most.
Fill the middle sections the most.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fill the middle sections the most.
questions.explanation: When filling a divided tank, do not put too much weight on the front or rear of the vehicle. Fill the middle sections the most to balance the load.

questions.question: A stopped bus is a concern because:

options.text: It is not a cause for concern.
It is not a concern if passengers are not getting off.
It should not be on the roadway.
Passengers may cross in front or behind it, and they may not see your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passengers may cross in front or behind it, and they may not see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front or behind it, and the bus may block their view of other traffic.

questions.question: When driving a tank vehicle, how should you take a highway curve?

options.text: At or slightly above the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have a high center of gravity and can easily roll over. On curves and ramps, drive well below the speed limit to reduce rollover risk.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn on, then shut off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on, then shut off quickly.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn on briefly, then turn off quickly.

questions.question: When placing a hazardous materials placard, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it at least three inches away from other markings.
Place it under a ladder if there is not enough space.
Place it on a background that matches its color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it at least three inches away from other markings.
questions.explanation: Placards must be at least three inches away from other markings, not under ladders, on a contrasting color background, and placed right-side up with words level and reading left to right.

questions.question: When going down a hill, how can you reduce brake use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, slow down and shift to a lower gear. This lets you control your vehicle without using the brakes too much. Using the brakes too much downhill can make them overheat and lose stopping power.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Never try to outdrive a train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never try to outdrive a train.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see a railroad crossing. You may not hear a train, and signals may not always warn you. Never try to drive faster than a train to cross the tracks.

questions.question: What is the best way to know your trailer is skidding?

options.text: By seeing it in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: By seeing it in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The earliest and best way to see a trailer skid is to watch your mirrors. You will see the trailer moving off course.

questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks hazardous to other drivers?

options.text: They must keep ice cream cold.
Children run toward them without looking for traffic.
They leave water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children run toward them without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks are dangerous because they attract children. Children often do not notice or watch for other vehicles when running to or from the truck.

questions.question: When entering a curve, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift.
questions.explanation: Take curves at a safe speed. Always downshift before entering a curve.
